title: How to Make Infused Honey | The Bridge
description: Honey isn't a fat, so this adult recipe starts with a spoonful of infused oil and a lot of stirring. Small batch, short life, loud label, locked away.
lede: Honey won't carry THC the way fat does, so this recipe starts with a spoonful of infused oil and a lot of stirring. Small batch, short life, loud label.
html:
Cannabinoids go where the fat is, and honey isn't a fat. Researchers describe THC and CBD as lipophilic, with a very high affinity for lipid particles. So this recipe doesn't steep flower in honey. It makes the infusion in oil, then works that oil into warm honey. For adults 21 and older, at home, and only if you can keep it locked.

Ingredients

  • 1 tablespoon freshly made infused olive oil, no more than a day old
  • 1/2 cup honey
  • 1/2 teaspoon sunflower lecithin, optional, to help the oil and honey stay together

You'll also need: a small heatproof jar, a pan of hot water, a small whisk or fork, a clean jar with a lid, a label and a lockbox.

Method

  1. Make the oil, following that recipe, and let it cool until just warm.
  2. Put the honey in the heatproof jar and stand it in the pan of hot water over low heat. You want it loose enough to pour. It should never simmer.
  3. Stir in the lecithin, if you're using it, until there are no clumps.
  4. Add the oil a few drops at a time, whisking hard the whole way. Once it's all in, keep going for five minutes. It should look cloudy and even.
  5. Pour into the clean jar. Label it right away: CONTAINS THC, ADULTS ONLY, made on this date, throw out on this date.
  6. Refrigerate it in the lockbox. Before each use, let it soften and stir it well, because oil and honey want to separate.

What's in a spoonful

You can't measure it at home. You can only find the ceiling. The oil recipe tops out at about 15 milligrams of THC per teaspoon if your flower tests at 20% Total THC, so the tablespoon you used holds at most about 44 milligrams. Spread through 1/2 cup of honey, 24 teaspoons, that's a ceiling of about 2 milligrams per teaspoon.

That sounds tidy, and it isn't. The real figure will be lower on average, and a jar that has separated could run stronger at the top than at the bottom. Start with one teaspoon, stirred, on a day with nowhere to be. New York's guidance says edibles may take up to two hours to feel, and four or more hours to be fully felt. Have no more that day. A spoonful stirred into hot tea is still an edible: when you eat or drink cannabis, the state says, it's broken down through the liver either way.

Skip the hot toddy. The state says cannabis and alcohol together can make you more impaired than either alone.

The four-day rule

The CDC's botulism guidance says to refrigerate homemade oils made with garlic or herbs and throw them away after 4 days. This honey is carrying a homemade herb oil, so we hold it to the same rule. Four days in the fridge, then it goes. That's why the batch is small.

Who this must never reach

A jar of honey reads as food to everybody in the house. The Department of Health says infused products should never be stored in a shared fridge or pantry near other food, and the state wants them locked. Keep the lockbox apart from the food, and never leave the jar out by the tea things. The CDC adds a rule for all honey: it is not safe for children younger than 1. If kids live with you and you can't guarantee the lock, don't make this.

When it's time to throw it out, follow the state's disposal sheet: mix it with coffee grounds or kitty litter, seal it in a container and put it in the regular trash, not down the sink. If anyone eats it by accident, call the Poison Center at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 in an emergency. For a pet, call your vet right away.
